tools.name: server_info
tools.description:
Return COMSOL MCP status and the recommended attach-first workflow.

    For normal visible Desktop usage, manually start COMSOL Multiphysics Server,
    connect Desktop to it, and then call server_connect().

tools.name: check_server_port
tools.description: Check whether a manually started COMSOL Server is listening on host:port.

tools.name: server_start
tools.description:
Advanced fallback only: start a local COMSOL server and connect MCP to it.

    Do NOT use this as the default visible workflow.
    Preferred workflow:
    1. Manually start COMSOL Multiphysics Server.
    2. Connect COMSOL Desktop to that server.
    3. Call server_connect(host, port) from MCP.

    Use server_start() only when MCP should own the COMSOL server lifecycle and
    random or non-default listening ports are acceptable.

tools.name: server_connect
tools.description:
Default entrypoint: attach MCP to an already running COMSOL Multiphysics Server.

    This is the recommended tool for the visible Desktop workflow:
    manually start COMSOL Multiphysics Server, call server_connect(host, port),
    load_visible_main_model(path), then connect Desktop and import that model.

tools.name: server_disconnect
tools.description: Disconnect the MCP client. Optionally shut down the local server if MCP started it.

tools.name: workflow_info
tools.description: Return the persisted MCP workflow policy for current-main-model operation.

tools.name: configure_single_main_workflow
tools.description:
Persist the single-current-main-model workflow in MCP state.

    model_dimension: spatial dimension of the model (2 or 3). Set to 0 to
    skip. This is used by create_physics and evaluate_expressions aggregate
    to select the correct COMSOL node types. For 2D models set to 2, for 3D
    set to 3.

tools.name: load_visible_main_model
tools.description: Load or adopt the visible main MPH, then lock MCP to that server-side model.

tools.name: start_visible_main_workflow
tools.description: Fixed visible workflow entrypoint: check port, connect, load MPH, then instruct Desktop import.

tools.name: start_visible_main_workflow_async
tools.description: Start visible-main loading in a background job so large MPH loads do not hit tool timeouts.

tools.name: visible_main_workflow_status
tools.description: Return status for the latest or specified asynchronous visible-main workflow job.

tools.name: verify_visible_main_session
tools.description: Verify that MCP is still operating on the locked visible main model.

tools.name: unlock_visible_main
tools.description: Unlock the visible-main guard for explicit maintenance actions.

tools.name: mcp_tool_audit
tools.description: Return the visible-main safety classification for the MCP tool surface.

tools.name: model_tree
tools.description: Return tags and structure for the current server-side model.

tools.name: run_study
tools.description: Run the current model study, optionally restricting execution to a study tag.

tools.name: load_current_main_model
tools.description: Load the persisted current main model into the connected COMSOL server session.

tools.name: model_create
tools.description: Create a new in-memory model on the connected COMSOL server and select it as current.

tools.name: model_load
tools.description: Load an MPH file on the connected COMSOL server and select it as current.

tools.name: prune_loaded_models
tools.description: Remove extra loaded server-side models and keep only the requested working model.

tools.name: get_parameters
tools.description: Return current global parameters from the selected server-side model.

tools.name: evaluate_expressions
tools.description:
Evaluate one or more expressions on the current server-side model.

    Each expression item supports: {"name": "...", "expression": "...",
      "aggregate": "max"|"min"|"avg"|"integral"|"none",
      "domains": [1,2], "boundaries": [5,6], "time_point": "last"|"all"|"N"}.

    Backward compatible: [{"name": "...", "expression": "..."}] still works.
    max_result_size: when > 0, truncate arrays exceeding this size (chars).

tools.name: get_core_metrics
tools.description: Return the core metrics used by the current short-window mainline.

tools.name: set_parameters
tools.description: Set multiple global parameters on the selected server-side model.

tools.name: ensure_component
tools.description: Ensure a component exists in the selected server-side model.

tools.name: ensure_geometry
tools.description: Ensure a geometry sequence exists in the selected server-side model.

tools.name: ensure_mesh
tools.description: Ensure a mesh sequence exists in the selected server-side model.

tools.name: create_feature
tools.description: Create a geometry feature and optionally apply initial properties.

tools.name: update_feature
tools.description: Update geometry feature properties on the selected server-side model.

tools.name: delete_feature
tools.description: Delete a geometry feature from the selected server-side model.

tools.name: run_feature
tools.description: Run a geometry or mesh sequence on the selected server-side model.

tools.name: run_visible_main_iteration
tools.description: Run one locked visible-main iteration: set parameters, solve, extract metrics, save a copy snapshot.

tools.name: save_main_model_snapshot
tools.description: Save a named snapshot from the current server-side model using the persisted workflow naming policy.

tools.name: commit_current_main_model
tools.description: Save a named snapshot, then overwrite the persisted current main model with the current server-side state.

tools.name: save_model
tools.description: Save the current server-side model to disk.

tools.name: list_physics
tools.description:
List all physics interfaces in a component with their features.

    Returns tags, labels, and feature counts for each physics interface.

tools.name: create_physics
tools.description:
Add a physics interface to a component.

    Common physics_type values: "cfpde" (Coefficient Form PDE),
    "tds" (Transport of Diluted Species), "solid" (Solid Mechanics),
    "ht" (Heat Transfer), "es" (Electrostatics), etc.

    dimension: spatial dimension (1, 2, or 3). Default 0 = auto-detect from
    the component's geometry. Set via configure_single_main_workflow(model_dimension=2).

    dependent_variables: comma-separated dependent variable names. Default "u".
    COMSOL uses these to create the correct physics with matching spatial dimension.
    For multiple dependent variables use "u,v" or "u,v,w".

tools.name: remove_physics
tools.description: Remove a physics interface from a component.

tools.name: list_physics_features
tools.description:
List all features (boundary conditions, sources, etc.) under a physics interface.

    Returns tags, labels, feature_type identifiers, property names, and
    selection editability for each feature. The feature_type field shows the
    COMSOL internal identifier to use with create_physics_feature.

tools.name: create_physics_feature
tools.description:
Add a child feature (boundary condition, source term, etc.) to a physics interface.

    IMPORTANT: feature_type uses COMSOL internal identifiers, NOT display names.
    For example, in TDS (Transport of Diluted Species), valid types include:
    "Inflow", "Outflow", "Flux", "NoFlux", "Concentration", "InitialValues",
    "ConservedQuantity", "WeakConstraint".
    Use list_physics_features first to discover existing feature_type identifiers
    in the current physics interface, as these vary per physics type and COMSOL version.
    properties_json format: [{"name": "prop_name", "value": "value"}] or
    {"prop_name": "value", ...}.

tools.name: update_physics_feature
tools.description:
Set properties on an existing physics feature.

    properties_json format: [{"name": "prop_name", "value": "value"}] or
    {"prop_name": "value", ...}. For array-valued properties use
    [{"name": "prop_name", "values": ["v1", "v2"]}].

tools.name: remove_physics_feature
tools.description: Remove a child feature from a physics interface.

tools.name: set_physics_selection
tools.description:
Set domain, boundary, or edge selection for a physics feature.

    entities_json is a JSON array of integer entity IDs, e.g. "[1, 2, 3]".
    Some features have inherited selections that cannot be modified directly.
    Use list_physics_features to check selection_editable before calling this.
    If selection is not editable on a feature, try setting it on the parent
    physics interface instead (pass the physics tag as feature_tag).

tools.name: manage_variables
tools.description:
Manage variable definitions: list, create, or remove.

    Actions:
    - "list": List all variables. Returns tags, names, and expressions.
    - "create": Create a variable node with given name and expression.
    - "remove": Remove a variable node by tag.

    When component is empty, operates on global variables.
    When component is specified, operates on component-level variables.

tools.name: list_solver_config
tools.description:
List all solver configurations with their features.

    Returns solver tags, feature counts, and feature tags for each solver
    configuration in the current model.

tools.name: create_solver_config
tools.description:
Create a solver configuration linked to a study.

    The solver tag identifies the new solver config. The study tag links it
    to an existing study for solving.

tools.name: list_solver_features
tools.description:
List features and sub-features under a solver configuration.

    Returns feature tags, labels, properties, and any sub-features (e.g.
    segregated solver steps).

tools.name: configure_solver
tools.description:
Configure a solver feature's properties.

    properties_json format: [{"name": "prop_name", "value": "value"}] or
    {"prop_name": "value", ...}. For array-valued properties use
    [{"name": "prop_name", "values": ["v1", "v2"]}].

    To add segregated solver steps, use properties_json with:
    [{"name": "add_segregated_step", "value": "{"step_tag": "step1", "variables": ["u", "v"]}"}]
    Multiple steps can be added in a single call.

tools.name: run_study_async
tools.description:
Run a COMSOL study in a background thread and return a job ID for polling.

    This is the async version of run_study. It starts the solve in a background
    thread and returns immediately with a job_id. Use run_study_status(job_id)
    to poll for completion.

    The MCP client will NOT disconnect during long solves because this tool
    returns immediately.

tools.name: run_study_status
tools.description:
Return status for the latest or specified async run_study job.

    Pass the job_id returned by run_study_async, or leave empty to get the
    latest job status.
